directAnswer: Pope John VI, a Greek, reigned from 701 to 705. The Liber Pontificalis records that he protected the exarch of Ravenna from hostile Italian troops, ransomed captives taken by the Lombard duke of Benevento, and upheld the appeal of St. Wilfrid of York.

sections.h2: Shielding the Exarch and Ransoming Captives
paras: John was of Greek origin; later lists say he came from the Greek East, possibly Asia Minor, though details of his early life are not recorded. Soon after his election, the exarch Theophylact arrived in Rome from Sicily, and militia troops from across imperial Italy gathered in a threatening mood. John shut the city gates, sent priests to calm the soldiers, and protected the exarch from harm, according to the Liber Pontificalis.

When Gisulf, the Lombard duke of Benevento, raided Campania, burning and taking captives, John sent clergy with gifts to ransom the prisoners and persuaded the duke to withdraw. The episode shows the pope acting as the main defender of the Roman region in the absence of effective imperial help.

sections.h2: The Final Appeal of Wilfrid of York
paras: In 704 the aged Wilfrid, still in conflict with English church authorities, appealed once more to Rome. A synod under John examined his case at length and found in his favor, and the pope wrote to the kings of Mercia and Northumbria urging that the matter be settled. John died on 11 January 705 and was buried in St. Peter's. Little else is known about him.

keyFacts: Protected the exarch Theophylact from mutinous Italian militia
Ransomed captives from Duke Gisulf of Benevento
Upheld St. Wilfrid's appeal at a Roman synod in 704

faqs.question: How did John VI defend Rome?
faqs.answer: He calmed militia troops threatening the exarch and paid ransom to the Lombard duke Gisulf of Benevento to free captives and persuade him to withdraw from Roman territory.

faqs.question: What was the outcome of Wilfrid's appeal to John VI?
faqs.answer: A Roman synod under John VI ruled in Wilfrid's favor, and the pope wrote to English kings asking them to resolve his case. Wilfrid was eventually reconciled and spent his last years in his monasteries.
